title: Short Stuff: Titanic Survivors!
summary: Short Stuff episode on the survivors of the Titanic sinking in April 1912. Josh and Chuck cover survival rates by sex and class (women about 74 percent, men about 20 percent; first class 62 percent, second class 43 percent, third class 26 percent, crew 24 percent), the women-and-children-first practice, and the poor conditions and flooding risk for lower-deck passengers. A detour about Usher's airport boarding is off-topic banter. They then profile notable survivors: Milvina Dean, the nine-week-old youngest survivor; Margaret "Molly" Brown, who helped organize aid on the Carpathia; Carl Behr and Richard Norris Williams, tennis players who later competed against each other; Edith Rosenbaum Russell and her toy pig; and Bruce Ismay, White Star Line managing director, who criticized for boarding a lifeboat.

segments.title: Opening banter
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck introduce the short stuff episode about Titanic survivors.

segments.title: Titanic voyage basics
segments.summary: Titanic left Southampton for New York on April 10, 1912, and sank on the night of April 14 into the 15th after striking an iceberg, with about 2,240 people aboard including 900 crew.

segments.title: Survival rates by sex and class
segments.summary: Seventy-four percent of female passengers and twenty percent of male passengers survived. Women and children first was applied, and Captain Edward John Smith reportedly ordered it. First class passengers had a 62 percent survival rate, helped by location near the lifeboats and quicker information.

segments.title: Second class and cabin conditions
segments.summary: Second class passengers had a 43 percent survival rate, as they were farther from lifeboats and crew paid them less attention. Some second class cabins were unfinished due to the rushed construction, with reports of leftover sandwiches from workmen.

segments.title: Off-topic airport boarding anecdote
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck trade stories about chaotic airplane boarding and a celebrity seen boarding a commercial flight. This is unrelated to Titanic.

segments.title: Third class survival and language barriers
segments.summary: Only 174 of 709 third class passengers survived, about 26 percent. Third class passengers were low on the ship, were not clearly instructed, and may have had a language barrier. Lower decks were the first to flood.

segments.title: Crew survival
segments.summary: Only about 24 percent of crew members survived, the lowest rate, many having died saving others.

segments.title: Milvina Dean
segments.summary: Milvina Dean, a nine-week-old from England, was the youngest Titanic survivor. Her family had been moved to the ship by a coal strike; her father died while her mother, brother and she survived. She later became the oldest living survivor, dying in 2009 at 97, and did not learn she was a Titanic passenger until age eight.

segments.title: Molly Brown
segments.summary: Margaret 'Molly' Brown helped organize survivors aboard the Carpathia, assisted Irish immigrants with language barriers, and raised about 10,000 dollars from first class passengers for second and third class survivors who lost family. The press's 'unsinkable Molly Brown' nickname was used although she was always called Margaret.

segments.title: Carl Behr and Richard Norris Williams
segments.summary: Tennis players Carl Behr and Richard Norris Williams both survived. Behr helped his fiancee Helen Newsom onto a lifeboat. Williams was rescued, and the two later competed against each other on the tennis court.

segments.title: Edith Rosenbaum Russell and the toy pig
segments.summary: Edith Rosenbaum, later Edith Rosenbaum Russell, became a fashion journalist and buyer. She carried a toy pig from her mother; a crew member threw the pig into a lifeboat and she followed it. The pig is in the National Maritime Museum in London.

segments.title: Bruce Ismay
segments.summary: Bruce Ismay, managing director of the White Star Line, survived by boarding one of the last lifeboats and faced criticism for it. The film portrayal was by Jonathan Hyde.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts close the episode with the standard sign-off and credits.
